_meta.description: Verified trough→peak close multiples for high-volatility stocks, archived from the Yahoo Finance v8 chart API. Every multiple is recomputable as peak.adjclose / trough.adjclose from values stored here; scripts/verify.py re-derives each one. All claims are window-bounded (extremum inside the documented fetch window), not all-time claims.
_meta.vendor_notice: Yahoo Finance is a commercial market-data vendor, NOT an official exchange, contest organiser or regulator. This module is deliberately separate from the official-source claims about the futures contest.
_meta.reverification_note: Second-pass re-verification 2026-09-16: all 16 endpoint windows (8 symbols x trough/peak) re-fetched from the Yahoo v8 chart API. All trough/peak dates and rounded multiples unchanged, except NVDA, whose archived endpoint values were re-adjusted by the vendor at the 6th decimal (trough 11.186728477478027 -> 11.186724662780762, peak 135.20559692382812 -> 135.20562744140625); the multiple still recomputes to 12.09x. See IR-13. Batch 2 (same date): 12 additional symbols captured (ENPH, AMD, MARA, CVNA, RIOT, NVAX, APP, SHOP, PLUG, NIO, PTON, HOOD) with the same window-bounded methodology: daily extremum windows plus monthly locator scans bounding neighbouring months; extremum dates were cross-checked against monthly-close anchors. CVNA's 5:1 (2026-05-08) and SHOP's 10:1 (2022-06-29) split events verified via the API's events=splits response.

contest_relevance_note: These are equity price returns over multi-year windows. The Leap (September 2026 edition) is a futures-only contest — 0 equities in the verified universe — so none of these tickers is tradeable in the contest. They document what extreme volatility looks like in real, verified market data and bound expectations: the largest verified multiple (382x, ENPH) took roughly 4.5 years, and the largest inside a single year was 119.85x (RIOT, 336 days).
